### Subject:FW: Study permit work eligibility question-REP-2017-2061

#### Hello

This is in response for your enquiry regarding the validity dates of study permits and eligibility of students to work after completion of their studies.

As per subsection R222(1), once an officer has determined that an applicant is bona fide and meets the requirements, they are to issue a long-term study permit, along with a long-term multiple-entry TRV or an eTA, if applicable, for the length of studies plus 90 days or passport expiry, whichever comes first.

Please note that the student must cease work as soon as they completed of their program of study and if they did not be applying for a work permit, as they are no longer eligible to work without a work permit under R186(v).

I hope that this information is helpful to you. If you have any further enquiries, you may contact us at ImmigrationRepresentatives@cic.gc.ca

Regards,

IMM 5814 does not appear in the "Form quick find" section. If the applicant selects "Study in Canada" under the "Temporary residence" section, the applicant can choose to apply online or on paper. If the applicant chooses to "Apply online for a study permit", they will simply be directed back to the online questionnaire that does not end up generating a "Study Plan" on the document checklist.

It is only if the applicant indicates that they will be applying on paper, that they will be prompted to first read IMM 5269 ("Applying for a Study Permit outside Canada). Applicants are also prompted to prepare their "application package" by selecting their country/territory, after which they will be able to obtain their local visa office instructions. These prompts are not, however, included for applicants who indicate that they will be applying online.

This summer (2017), we were contacted by several of our incoming students from Pakistan who received Study Permit refusals. All of them had applied online and none of them had submitted a Study Plan, as they had not been prompted to do so. The reasons for the refusal usually included doubts about the purpose of visit, whether the applicant was a bona fide student, whether the applicant would leave Canada after their studies, and the applicant's ties to his or her country of residence/citizenship. These are all issues that could have been addressed in the Study Plan. Given the timing of the refusals, these applicants were unable to attend or the Fall 2017 semester. Due to the nature of some programs, some of the students will have to defer the start of their studies for one full year.

Given the discrepancy between the information asked of online versus paper based Study Permit applications for applicants from Pakistan, along with the refusals we saw for online applications, we would greatly appreciate answers to the following questions:

1. Whether or not citizens of Pakistan who apply online for their Study Permit application are expected to include a Study Plan?
2. If so, how does IRCC ensure that students are aware of this expectation?
3. If students are expected to submit a Study Plan and IRCC does not currently prompt online applicants to submit a Study Plan, will changes be made to the way the personalized document checklist is generated to ensure that these applicants are aware that they must submit a Study Plan with their application?

## Hellc

This is in response to your enquiry sent on July 7 regarding study permit requirements for a minor outside of Canada.

As per our PDl on study permits and minor children, the exemption for requiring a study permit as a minor outlined in A30(2) only applies to minors already in Canada. As a result, minors intending to study are required to apply for a study permit before arriving at a port of entry in Canada.

I hope that this information is helpful to you. If you have any further enquiries, you may contact us at ImmigrationRepresentatives@cic.gc.ca.

Dear Mr. We regret the delay in responding to your enquiry. Thank you for taking the time to provide these comments. We are committed to making improvements wherever possible. Since publishing the new application kits in December 2016, we have been listening to feedback and input from both clients and representatives and working on updates to the application checklists and guides, which will be published shortly. From: ImmigrationRepresentatives <ImmigrationRepresentatives@cic.gc.ca> Date: Monday, January 23, 2017 at 2:20 PM To: Cc: ImmigrationRepresentatives <ImmigrationRepresentatives@cic.gc.ca> Subject: FW: Spousal Sponsorship-Document Checklist-REP-2017-0027-

## Dear Ms.

Thank you for your inquiry about the interpretation of Spousal Sponsorship information that is requested on the IMM 5589 (Document Checklist – Common-law partner). A link to this checklist is found here: [http://www.cic.gc.ca/english/pdf/kits/forms/IMM5589E.pdf](http://www.cic.gc.ca/english/pdf/kits/forms/IMM5589E.pdf)

Most applicants and sponsors who are cohabiting should be able to submit at least one important document showing the same address. However, if an applicant is not able to provide documentation from two of the three sets of options for proof of cohabitation (for example, if the applicant and sponsor have neither any joint utilities accounts, nor any indication of joint ownership, leasing, or occupation of accommodation), the applicant should instead provide a detailed written explanation of why this documentation is not available. Along with the explanation, he/she should provide any other evidence of cohabitation which is available (some examples may include documents for each individual with a common address listed-cell phone bills, pay stubs, tax forms, bank or credit card statements, etc.). The explanation and other submissions will be reviewed as part of the assessment of the application.

Thank you again for writing. We trust that this information will be of assistance.

Regards,

Just to clarify, super visa holders are eligible for a two-year stay on their initial entry ONLY. The same rule applies for visa-exempt parents and grandparents who present the super visa letter of introduction upon arrival at a Canadian port of entry. Once super visa holders (including visa-exempt super visa applicants) leave Canada and seek re-entry, Border Services Officers will assess them as regular visitors, pursuant to section 183 of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations. The super visa offers parents and grandparents the possibility of visiting Canada for up to two years on their initial stay only. Regulation 183(2) would apply to subsequent entries. When a super visa holder enters Canada for the first time and no admissibility issues are identified, the officer should stamp and write the date (2 year stay) in the passport. Should no date be affixed, R183 (2) would apply in that the period of authorized stay would be 6 months. Ultimately Border Services Officer at the POE have the authority to determine the length of time that a temporary resident may remain in Canada. We hope this information will be helpful to you.

### Zare.Atabak From:ImmigrationRepresentatives

### Sent:Tuesday, March 14, 2017 2:20 PM

To:

## Cc: ImmigrationRepresentatives Subject:FW: Supervisa "extension" REP-2017-0419-

## Good day,

Foreign nationals who do not require a temporary resident visa to enter Canada who wish to benefit from the super visa program, must complete and submit the requested documents as outlined on our website at the following link: [http://www.cic.gc.ca/english/visit/supervisa-how.asp](http://www.cic.gc.ca/english/visit/supervisa-how.asp). If the application is approved they will be provided with a letter of introduction that can be presented at the port of entry where a Border Services Officer may approve a visit to Canada for up to two years. It is important to note that super visa holder are eligible for a two-year stay on their initial visit only.

Super visa clients in Canada who have valid temporary status may apply to extend their status from within Canada. As with all temporary residents seeking extension, super visa clients are assessed as regular visitors. The length of the extension is at the discretion of the processing officer. Detailed application instructions can be found here: [http://www.cic.gc.ca/english/information/applications/visitor.asp](http://www.cic.gc.ca/english/information/applications/visitor.asp).

If the extension as a visitor is granted, an immigration document will be sent to the client which will indicate the date which they must leave Canada. If the application is refused, the cliebt can only stay in Canada until the expiry date of their current temporary resident status.

Regards,

The Immigration Representatives Mailbox
